paragraphs.text: Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Prosechete de tēn dikaiosynēn hymōn mē poiein emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn pros to theathēnai autois· ei de mē ge, misthon ouk echete para tō patri hymōn tō en tois ouranois.

i18n.en: Take care not to practice your righteousness before people in order to be seen by them; for if you do, you have no reward from your Father who is in the heavens.

notes.official: *prosechete tēn dikaiosynēn hymōn mē poiein emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn* — 'beware of practicing your righteousness before others'. The Matthean redactional-hinge introducing the three-fold piety-section (alms / prayer / fasting) where each piety-practice is treated against the *hypokrisis* (public-display) anti-pattern. The Matthean Jesus' critique targets ostentatious-piety, not the practices themselves.

paragraphs.text: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Hotan oun poiēs eleēmosynēn, mē salpisēs emprosthen sou, hōsper hoi hypokritai poiousin en tais synagōgais kai en tais rhymais, hopōs doxasthōsin hypo tōn anthrōpōn· amēn legō hymin, apechousin ton misthon autōn.

i18n.en: So when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may be praised by people. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.

notes.official: *hypokritai* — 'hypocrites', literally 'actors' (one playing-a-role on stage). The Matthean technical term for the public-display anti-pattern. The critique is intra-Jewish (the Matthean community is Jewish-Christian) and addresses the temptation to ostentatious-piety; the supersessionist generalization 'Jews are hypocrites' is a downstream Christian-anti-Judaic misreading. Davies-Allison ICC 1.578-580.

paragraphs.text: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου,
paragraphs.translit: sou de poiountos eleēmosynēn mē gnōtō hē aristera sou ti poiei hē dexia sou,

i18n.en: But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

paragraphs.text: ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
paragraphs.translit: hopōs ē sou hē eleēmosynē en tō kryptō· kai ho patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryptō apodōsei soi.

i18n.en: so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hotan proseuchēsthe, ouk esesthe hōs hoi hypokritai· hoti philousin en tais synagōgais kai en tais gōniais tōn plateiōn hestōtes proseuchesthai, hopōs phanōsin tois anthrōpois· amēn legō hymin, apechousin ton misthon autōn.

i18n.en: And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and at the street corners, that they may be seen by people. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.

notes.official: *hotan proseuchēsthe ... ouk esesthe hōs hoi hypokritai* — the prayer-section opens with the same *hypokritai* warning against public-display. Cross-corpus to the Qumran Hodayot communal-prayer tradition; the Pharisaic-rabbinic tradition itself develops critiques of ostentatious-piety (m.Sotah 3:4 the seven-types-of-Pharisees).

paragraphs.text: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
paragraphs.translit: sy de hotan proseuchē, eiselthe eis to tameion sou kai kleisas tēn thyran sou proseuxai tō patri sou tō en tō kryptō· kai ho patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryptō apodōsei soi.

i18n.en: But you, when you pray, go into your inner room, and shutting your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.

paragraphs.text: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί, δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: Proseuchomenoi de mē battalogēsēte hōsper hoi ethnikoi, dokousin gar hoti en tē polylogia autōn eisakousthēsontai.

i18n.en: And in praying, do not babble as the Gentiles do, for they think they will be heard for their many words.

paragraphs.text: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς, οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: mē oun homoiōthēte autois, oiden gar ho patēr hymōn hōn chreian echete pro tou hymas aitēsai auton.

i18n.en: Therefore do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.

paragraphs.text: Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου,
paragraphs.translit: Houtōs oun proseuchesthe hymeis· Pater hēmōn ho en tois ouranois, hagiasthētō to onoma sou,

i18n.en: Pray then in this way: Our Father who are in the heavens, hallowed be your name,

notes.official: **The Lord's Prayer opens.** *Pater hēmōn ho en tois ouranois* — 'our Father in the heavens'. Cross-corpus to the Jewish liturgical-tradition: *Avinu she-ba-shamayim* (Our Father in heaven), the Kaddish opening *yitgadal we-yitkadash shemeh rabba* (may his great name be magnified and sanctified). *hagiasthētō to onoma sou* directly echoes the Kaddish sanctification. The Matthean Lord's Prayer is rooted in Jewish liturgical-prayer structures. See `lords-prayer-mt-6-9-13-pater-hēmōn-byzantine-doxology-textual-variant-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: elthetō hē basileia sou, genēthētō to thelēma sou, hōs en ouranō kai epi gēs.

i18n.en: your kingdom come, your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.

notes.official: *eltheto hē basileia sou; genēthētō to thelēma sou* — 'your kingdom come; your will be done'. Echoes the Kaddish's *we-yamlikh malkhuteh* ('and may he establish his kingship'); echoes 1 Macc 3:60 *hōs an ē thelēma en ouranō, houtōs poiēsei* ('as may be the will in heaven, so shall he do'). See `kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`.

paragraphs.text: Τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·
paragraphs.translit: Ton arton hēmōn ton epiousion dos hēmin sēmeron·

i18n.en: Give us this day our daily bread;

notes.official: *ton arton hēmōn ton epiousion* — the *epiousios* hapax legomenon (unattested in pre-NT Greek). Three competing renderings: 'daily' (the dominant English-tradition); 'for-tomorrow' (Jerome's Lk 11:3 'crastinum'; Jeremias 1971 reconstruction from Aramaic *yoma de-yatya*); 'supersubstantial' (Jerome's Mt 6:11 'supersubstantialem'; the Catholic Eucharistic-reading). The WoH-Translation preserves 'daily' per the dominant convention; see overlay entry `epiousios-hapax-translation-convention`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: kai aphes hēmin ta opheilēmata hēmōn, hōs kai hēmeis aphēkamen tois opheiletais hēmōn·

i18n.en: and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors;

notes.official: *ta opheilēmata hēmōn* — 'our debts' (literal-financial-debt metaphor for sin). The Matthean choice of *opheilēmata* (vs Lukan *hamartias* 'sins' at Lk 11:4) preserves the Aramaic *ḥobaʾ* (debt-as-sin metaphor) more directly. The forgive-as-we-forgive conditional is a distinctive Matthean theological-feature reinforced at Mt 6:14-15 and Mt 18:23-35 (the unforgiving-servant parable).

paragraphs.text: καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai mē eisenenkēs hēmas eis peirasmon, alla rhysai hēmas apo tou ponērou.

i18n.en: and do not bring us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.

notes.official: *mē eisenenkēs hēmas eis peirasmon, alla rhysai hēmas apo tou ponērou* — 'do not lead us into testing, but deliver us from the evil one'. *peirasmos* covers both 'testing/trial' (eschatological-testing) and 'temptation' (moral-seduction); the eschatological-testing sense is the more-likely Matthean horizon. *tou ponērou* admits masculine 'the evil one' (Satan) or neuter 'evil' generically; the masculine reading is supported by Mt 13:19, 13:38. **Textual variant:** the Byzantine doxology *hoti sou estin hē basileia kai hē dynamis kai hē doxa eis tous aiōnas, amēn* is absent in B + א + critical text. See overlay entry `lords-prayer-doxology-textual-variant-convention`.

paragraphs.text: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·
paragraphs.translit: ean gar aphēte tois anthrōpois ta paraptōmata autōn, aphēsei kai hymin ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios·

i18n.en: For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;

paragraphs.text: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ean de mē aphēte tois anthrōpois, oude ho patēr hymōn aphēsei ta paraptōmata hymōn.

i18n.en: but if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

paragraphs.text: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί, ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Hotan de nēsteuēte, mē ginesthe hōs hoi hypokritai skythrōpoi, aphanizousin gar ta prosōpa autōn hopōs phanōsin tois anthrōpois nēsteuontes· amēn legō hymin, apechousin ton misthon autōn.

i18n.en: And when you fast, do not be gloomy-faced like the hypocrites; for they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by people to be fasting. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.

notes.official: *hotan de nēsteuēte ... hōs hoi hypokritai* — the fasting-section, closing the three-fold piety-pattern. Cross-corpus to Isa 58:1-9 (the prophetic critique of ostentatious-fasting and the call for justice-as-true-fasting). Davies-Allison ICC 1.616-620.

paragraphs.text: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι,
paragraphs.translit: sy de nēsteuōn aleipsai sou tēn kephalēn kai to prosōpon sou nipsai,

i18n.en: But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,

paragraphs.text: ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.
paragraphs.translit: hopōs mē phanēs tois anthrōpois nēsteuōn alla tō patri sou tō en tō kryphaiō· kai ho patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryphaiō apodōsei soi.

i18n.en: so that you may not be seen by people to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.

paragraphs.text: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: Mē thēsaurizete hymin thēsaurous epi tēs gēs, hopou sēs kai brōsis aphanizei, kai hopou kleptai dioryssousin kai kleptousin·

i18n.en: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break in and steal;

notes.official: *mē thēsaurizete hymin thēsaurous epi tēs gēs* — 'do not store up treasures on earth'. The treasure-in-heaven teaching has cross-corpus parallels: Sir 29:11 'lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High'; Tob 4:8-9 (Tobit's almsgiving-treasure-in-heaven counsel); 4 Ezra 6:5; 7:77 (the apocalyptic-treasury-of-merit tradition). The Matthean teaching is rooted in Jewish-wisdom tradition.

paragraphs.text: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: thēsaurizete de hymin thēsaurous en ouranō, hopou oute sēs oute brōsis aphanizei, kai hopou kleptai ou dioryssousin oude kleptousin·

i18n.en: but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumes, and where thieves do not break in or steal.

paragraphs.text: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου.
paragraphs.translit: hopou gar estin ho thēsauros sou, ekei estai kai hē kardia sou.

i18n.en: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

paragraphs.text: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός. ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·
paragraphs.translit: Ho lychnos tou sōmatos estin ho ophthalmos. ean oun ē ho ophthalmos sou haplous, holon to sōma sou phōteinon estai·

i18n.en: The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light;

notes.official: *ho lychnos tou sōmatos estin ho ophthalmos* — the eye-as-lamp-of-the-body saying. The *ophthalmos haplous* (single/healthy eye) vs *ponēros* (evil/bad eye) is rooted in Jewish-tradition: a *haplous*/single eye marks generosity (Sir 32:8; T. Iss. 3:4); an *ophthalmos ponēros*/evil eye marks envy/stinginess (Deut 15:9 *ʿênĕkā ḥātĕṭâ ʾāḥîkā* 'your eye is begrudging toward your brother'; Prov 23:6; 28:22).

paragraphs.text: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.
paragraphs.translit: ean de ho ophthalmos sou ponēros ē, holon to sōma sou skoteinon estai. ei oun to phōs to en soi skotos estin, to skotos poson.

i18n.en: but if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!

paragraphs.text: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
paragraphs.translit: Oudeis dynatai dysi kyriois douleuein· ē gar ton hena misēsei kai ton heteron agapēsei, ē henos anthexetai kai tou heterou kataphronēsei. ou dynasthe theō douleuein kai mamōna.

i18n.en: No one is able to serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.

notes.official: *oudeis dynatai dysi kyriois douleuein ... ou dynasthe theō douleuein kai mamōna* — 'you cannot serve God and mammon'. *mamōnas* is an Aramaic loan-word (*māmôn* 'wealth, property'), preserved untranslated by Matthew. The Aramaic-loan-preservation parallel to *rhaka* at 5:22, *amēn* throughout, *kephas* in Pauline tradition.

paragraphs.text: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν· μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε ἢ τί πίητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;
paragraphs.translit: Dia touto legō hymin· mē merimnate tē psychē hymōn ti phagēte ē ti piēte, mēde tō sōmati hymōn ti endysēsthe· ouchi hē psychē pleion estin tēs trophēs kai to sōma tou endymatos?

i18n.en: Therefore I say to you, do not be anxious about your life, what you shall eat or what you shall drink; nor about your body, what you shall put on. Is not the life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

notes.official: *mē merimnate tē psychē hymōn* — 'do not be anxious for your life'. The anxiety-section (vv.25-34) is rooted in Jewish-wisdom (Sir 30:21-25; Sir 38:18-19 on care-and-anxiety; Ps 55:22; Prov 12:25) and addresses peasant-Galilean economic-anxiety in concrete terms. Davies-Allison ICC 1.647-656.

paragraphs.text: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;
paragraphs.translit: emblepsate eis ta peteina tou ouranou hoti ou speirousin oude therizousin oude synagousin eis apothēkas, kai ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios trephei auta· ouch hymeis mallon diapherete autōn?

i18n.en: Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow, nor reap, nor gather into barns; and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they?

paragraphs.text: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;
paragraphs.translit: tis de ex hymōn merimnōn dynatai prostheinai epi tēn hēlikian autou pēchyn hena?

i18n.en: And which of you by being anxious is able to add one cubit to his span of life?

paragraphs.text: καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε; καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν·
paragraphs.translit: kai peri endymatos ti merimnate? katamathete ta krina tou agrou pōs auxanousin· ou kopiōsin oude nēthousin·

i18n.en: And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not toil nor spin;

paragraphs.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
paragraphs.translit: legō de hymin hoti oude Solomōn en pasē tē doxē autou periebaleto hōs hen toutōn.

i18n.en: yet I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.

paragraphs.text: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;
paragraphs.translit: ei de ton chorton tou agrou sēmeron onta kai aurion eis klibanon ballomenon ho theos houtōs amphiennysin, ou pollō mallon hymas, oligopistoi?

i18n.en: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?

paragraphs.text: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν; ἤ· Τί πίωμεν; ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;
paragraphs.translit: mē oun merimnēsēte legontes· Ti phagōmen? ē· Ti piōmen? ē· Ti peribalōmetha?

i18n.en: Therefore do not be anxious, saying, "What shall we eat?" or "What shall we drink?" or "What shall we wear?"

paragraphs.text: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.
paragraphs.translit: panta gar tauta ta ethnē epizētousin· oiden gar ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios hoti chrēzete toutōn hapantōn.

i18n.en: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.

paragraphs.text: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: zēteite de prōton tēn basileian kai tēn dikaiosynēn autou, kai tauta panta prostethēsetai hymin.

i18n.en: But seek first the kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you.

notes.official: *zēteite de prōton tēn basileian kai tēn dikaiosynēn autou* — 'seek first the kingdom and his righteousness'. The Matthean *basileia* + *dikaiosynē* pairing closes the anxiety-discourse with the central Matthean theological-pair: the kingdom-of-the-heavens (the eschatological reign) + righteousness (the SM-ethical-program).

paragraphs.text: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει ἑαυτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: mē oun merimnēsēte eis tēn aurion, hē gar aurion merimnēsei heautēs· arketon tē hēmera hē kakia autēs.

i18n.en: Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.

notes.official: *arketon tē hēmera hē kakia autēs* — 'sufficient for the day is its own evil'. Closing-aphorism; rooted in Jewish-wisdom (cf. Sir 11:23-24).
